question:
A 75-year-old man presents to the physician with a complaint of persistent back pain. The patient states that the pain has been constant and occurs throughout the day. He says that he has also been experiencing greater fatigue when carrying out his daily activities. On review of systems, the patient notes that he lost more than 10 pounds in the past month despite maintaining his usual diet and exercising less often due to his fatigue. Physical exam is notable for a systolic murmur at the right sternal border, mild crackles at the bases of both lungs, and tenderness to palpation of his lumbar spine. Laboratory values are below:

Serum:
Na+: 141 mEq/L
Cl-: 101 mEq/L
K+: 4.2 mEq/L
HCO3-: 23 mEq/L
BUN: 20 mg/dL
Glucose: 101 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.6 mg/dL
Ca2+: 12.8 mg/dL

A peripheral blood smear is ordered for the patient’s work-up. Which of the following would be the most likely finding on peripheral blood smear?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "75-year-old man with persistent back pain" -> "weight loss of more than 10 pounds" -> "fatigue during daily activities" -> "systolic murmur at right sternal border" -> "mild crackles at lung bases" -> "elevated calcium level (12.8 mg/dL)" -> "possible malignancy or multiple myeloma" -> "peripheral blood smear ordered" -> "expected finding of rouleaux formation due to increased serum proteins" -> 85%

CHAIN: "75-year-old man with persistent back pain" -> "significant weight loss" -> "fatigue and decreased activity" -> "elevated calcium level (12.8 mg/dL)" -> "possible underlying hematological disorder" -> "peripheral blood smear ordered" -> "increased immunoglobulins leading to rouleaux formation" -> 80%

CHAIN: "75-year-old man with back pain and fatigue" -> "weight loss and elevated calcium" -> "suspected multiple myeloma" -> "peripheral blood smear ordered" -> "common finding in multiple myeloma is rouleaux formation" -> 90%

CHAIN: "75-year-old man with systemic symptoms" -> "elevated calcium level" -> "possible hematological malignancy" -> "peripheral blood smear ordered" -> "expected finding of rouleaux formation due to high protein levels" -> 75%
analysis: The patient presents with hypercalcemia (Ca2+ of 12.8 mg/dL), which can be associated with multiple myeloma. The symptoms of persistent back pain, fatigue, weight loss, and the presence of a systolic murmur suggest possible underlying malignancy or hematological disorder. In multiple myeloma, a common finding on peripheral blood smear is rouleaux formation due to increased plasma proteins. Therefore, the most likely finding on peripheral blood smear in this case is rouleaux formation.
